summary: The candidate is correct. The row-mass and incidence count give the claimed uniform cosh bound, and concavity of squared arcosh gives (7). Reflection orbits, the exact original-law factorization, and Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz establish (8)--(9), including singleton and lower-dimensional supports. Completeness and midpoint log-concavity justify the parity estimate and (12)--(14). The final obstruction-family checks preserve the supplied predecessor definitions and normalizations: the three-layer core has incidence one and unbounded row size, and the stronger family contains the stated growing reflected fiber. Small supports, zero variances, arbitrary positive weights, overlapping rows, and the halfspace boundary case introduce no error or gap.
